item.title: Cavan man says Irish flag is a symbol of survival
item.description: A Cavan man has been taking part in a debate relating to use of the Irish tricolour as a symbol of protest. Former Garda and whistleblower John Wilson was speaking on the Joe Finnegan show in response to an email from a listener upset after a number of tricolours "appeared out of nowhere" in Roscommon Town over the weekend. item.title: 'Significant revamp' for bank facilities in Ballybay
item.description: A significant revamp has been announced for the Bank of Ireland branch in Ballybay. Local Fianna Fáil Cllr, Seamus Coyle said that work will began in the branch in January 2026, and is due to be completed by early February 2026. Cllr. Coyle highlighted that a "brand new" ATM will also be in place in the town. Advertisement He said that the lack of an ATM in the town has been a huge inconvenience to local people. item.title: Road closed due to Stradone crash
item.description: A road has been closed in Co Cavan this afternoon following a road traffic collision. The R165 is currently closed north of Laragh House following a collision between a bus and a car. One person has been brough to hospital by ambulance. Advertisement Motorists should avoid the area for the present.

item.title: Man further remanded over fatal Co Monaghan crash
item.description: 56-year-old man has been further remanded in jail in relation to a fatal collision in Co Monaghan. Ion Bucurica appeared at Monaghan District Court charged with dangerous driving causing the death of the mother of two, Emma Mackeral. The Romanian national who resides in France appeared in front of Judge Gerard Jones at a special sitting of Monaghan District Court on Friday night and again this afternoon over the alleged offence. item.title: Refugee living in Co Monaghan says system has 'failed' her
item.description: A Ukrainian refugee living in Co Monaghan says the system has failed her. Maria Alekseeva who resides at the M Hotel in Carrickmacross says after she sought asylum she can't take up any employment. She says after seeking asylum here to remain in Ireland, she has been unable to obtain official identification so she can work here. item.title: Cavan food producer achieves nationwide recognition with ALDI
item.description: A Co Cavan producer has been crowned winner of Grow with ALDI 2025, with products hitting shelves nationwide from early next month. Barry John Sausages is set to launch in all 166 ALDI stores nationwide from January 8th. The announcement comes as ALDI opens applications for the 2026 programme, inviting innovative Irish food producers to apply by January 30th for the chance to bring their products to shelves across the country.
